claims.claim: ⚠️ **With red flag features, or vomiting without diarrhoea, consider alternative diagnoses.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Red flags:** younger than 6 months · haematemesis · bilious vomiting · more than 10 days of diarrhoea · severe abdominal pain · refusal to walk · past GI/surgical history · complex medical history · post organ transplant · immunocompromise · re-presentation or failure to respond to standard therapy.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vomiting may precede diarrhoea by 24–48 hours**, but a vomiting child without diarrhoea needs other causes considered.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Blood or mucus in the stool** suggests significant inflammation, as with bacterial infection or inflammatory bowel conditions.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess the degree of dehydration** — it sets the route and rate of rehydration. Weigh the child (bare in infants).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Knowing the cause rarely changes management**, whether viral or bacterial.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most children with presumed, uncomplicated gastroenteritis need no investigations**, including stool testing.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Every child on IV fluids: check serum electrolytes and glucose before starting** (typically at cannulation) **and repeated within 24 hours** while IV therapy continues.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **BGL, ketones and electrolytes may also be needed** with severe dehydration, profuse or prolonged losses, altered conscious state, hypertonic or prolonged hypotonic fluid intake, complex comorbidities or diuretic use. **Ketotic hypoglycaemia can follow vomiting**, more often in younger children.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stool culture or viral testing is not advised**; exceptions are bloody diarrhoea in a young infant or an unwell child · a returned traveller with symptoms over 10 days · fever in an immunocompromised patient.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Many cases settle on their own**, needing only encouragement to drink and a watch on hydration. **Failure of initial management should prompt a rethink of the diagnosis.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral rehydration: target 10 mL/kg/hr of ORS (oral rehydration solution).**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mildly dehydrated child refusing ORS:** a short-term flavoured ice block, or apple juice diluted 1:1 with water.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stop any feed fortification.** **Continue breastfeeding, more often**, with extra ORS if appropriate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If oral rehydration fails, use rapid or slow NG rehydration**; if NG is not tolerated in a clinically dehydrated child, **move to IV**. In older children, IV can be the preferred route when NG is unsuitable or not tolerated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ondansetron** may support hydration in children and infants **over 6 months** with persistent nausea or vomiting.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Initial oral ondansetron by weight:** **2 mg** for 8–15 kg · **4 mg** for 15–30 kg · **8 mg** above 30 kg. **Ongoing dosing is 0.15 mg/kg.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **A response to anti-emetics does not confirm the diagnosis.** Other anti-emetics are not routinely recommended because of side effects.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **No anti-spasmodics or anti-diarrhoeals.** Evidence is insufficient to support probiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Reserve antibiotics** for enteritis-associated sepsis, selected cases with a specific bacterial pathogen (eg *Salmonella* Typhi; non-typhoidal salmonella under 3 months, immunocompromised or septic) or severe *C. difficile* infection.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Once rehydrated, restart a normal diet.** Do not routinely restrict lactose; consider it only if stool frequency increases. Diarrhoea may persist.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when** vomiting has reduced and the child is tolerating adequate oral fluids, with nil or mild dehydration.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve the paediatric team** if initial rehydration fails or losses are significant, with complex comorbidities, electrolyte abnormalities, an unclear diagnosis or red flags.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider transfer** for severe electrolyte disturbance or **shock needing 40 mL/kg of fluid boluses**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Gastroenteritis' (Last updated August 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Gastroenteritis/, retrieved 2026-09-23
